\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{হুঁশিয়ার} (hũshiyār)}{হুঁশিয়ার (hũshiyār)}]{\bn{হুঁশিয়ার} (hũshiyār) — watchful; on one's guard}

\label{lesson:BN-C374-hushiyar}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Bengali for nearly, then the Bengali for partial.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{হুঁশিয়ার}}
\textbf{\bn{হুঁশিয়ার}} — \emph{hũshiyār} — \textquotedblleft{}watchful; on one's guard\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\bn{রাতে} \bn{বাইরে} \bn{গেলে} \bn{হুঁশিয়ার} \bn{থেকো।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{rāte bāire gele hũshiyār theko.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Be on your guard if you go out at night.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\bn{হুঁশিয়ার}} (\emph{hũshiyār}) is usually traced to Persian \emph{hushyār}, alert or wide awake. As a single word it is also a warning: \bn{হুঁশিয়ার}! Watch out!
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{hũshiyār}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{hũshiyār}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{rāte bāire gele hũshiyār theko.} — Be on your guard if you go out at night.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Bengali for nearly, then the Bengali for partial, then say \emph{hũshiyār} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \bn{হুঁশিয়ার} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Watchful; on one's guard\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{প্রতিরোধ} \bn{করা} (prôtirodh kôrā)}{প্রতিরোধ করা (prôtirodh kôrā)}]{\bn{প্রতিরোধ} \bn{করা} (prôtirodh kôrā) — to resist; to prevent}

\label{lesson:BN-C374-protirodh-kora}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Bengali for partial, then the Bengali for on one's guard.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{প্রতিরোধ} \bn{করা}}
\textbf{\bn{প্রতিরোধ} \bn{করা}} — \emph{prôtirodh kôrā} — \textquotedblleft{}to resist; to prevent\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\bn{নিয়মিত} \bn{হাত} \bn{ধুলে} \bn{তুমি} \bn{অনেক} \bn{রোগ} \bn{প্রতিরোধ} \bn{করতে} \bn{পারবে।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{niyômitô hāt dhule tumi ônek rog prôtirodh kôrte pārbe.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
If you wash your hands regularly, you can ward off many diseases.
\end{quote}

Past (he/she …): \bn{তিনি} \bn{শত্রুকে} \bn{প্রতিরোধ} \bn{করলেন}, \emph{tini shôtruke prôtirodh kôrlen}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\bn{প্রতিরোধ} \bn{করা}} (\emph{prôtirodh kôrā}) is Sanskrit \emph{pratirodha}, opposition or obstruction (Monier-Williams), with \bn{করা}: to stand against an attack, a disease or a change.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{prôtirodh kôrā}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{prôtirodh kôrā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{niyômitô hāt dhule tumi ônek rog prôtirodh kôrte pārbe.} — If you wash your hands regularly, you can ward off many diseases.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Bengali for partial, then the Bengali for on one's guard, then say \emph{prôtirodh kôrā} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \bn{প্রতিরোধ} \bn{করা} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To resist; to prevent\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{ঠেকানো} (ṭhekāno)}{ঠেকানো (ṭhekāno)}]{\bn{ঠেকানো} (ṭhekāno) — to stop; to ward off}

\label{lesson:BN-C374-thekano}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Bengali for on one's guard, then the Bengali for to resist.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{ঠেকানো}}
\textbf{\bn{ঠেকানো}} — \emph{ṭhekāno} — \textquotedblleft{}to stop; to ward off\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\bn{দরজা} \bn{বন্ধ} \bn{না} \bn{করলে} \bn{তুমি} \bn{মশা} \bn{ঠেকাতে} \bn{পারবে} \bn{না।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{dôrjā bôndhô nā kôrle tumi môshā ṭhekāte pārbe nā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
If you don't close the door, you won't keep the mosquitoes out.
\end{quote}

Past (he/she …): \bn{তিনি} \bn{বলটা} \bn{ঠেকালেন}, \emph{tini bôlṭā ṭhekālen}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\bn{ঠেকানো}} (\emph{ṭhekāno}) is built on the reconstructed \emph{ṭhēkk}, to fix; CDIAL 5509 lists Bengali ṭhek, a prop, and ṭhekāna, to obstruct: to put something in the way so a thing cannot get through.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ṭhekāno}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ṭhekāno}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{dôrjā bôndhô nā kôrle tumi môshā ṭhekāte pārbe nā.} — If you don't close the door, you won't keep the mosquitoes out.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Bengali for on one's guard, then the Bengali for to resist, then say \emph{ṭhekāno} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \bn{ঠেকানো} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To stop; to ward off\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{নিয়ন্ত্রণ} \bn{করা} (niyôntrôn kôrā)}{নিয়ন্ত্রণ করা (niyôntrôn kôrā)}]{\bn{নিয়ন্ত্রণ} \bn{করা} (niyôntrôn kôrā) — to control}

\label{lesson:BN-C374-niyontron-kora}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Bengali for to resist, then the Bengali for to ward off.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{নিয়ন্ত্রণ} \bn{করা}}
\textbf{\bn{নিয়ন্ত্রণ} \bn{করা}} — \emph{niyôntrôn kôrā} — \textquotedblleft{}to control\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\bn{রাগ} \bn{নিয়ন্ত্রণ} \bn{না} \bn{করলে} \bn{বিপদ} \bn{হবে।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{rāg niyôntrôn nā kôrle bipôd hôbe.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
If you don't control your anger, there will be trouble.
\end{quote}

Past (he/she …): \bn{তিনি} \bn{ভিড়} \bn{নিয়ন্ত্রণ} \bn{করলেন}, \emph{tini bhiṛ niyôntrôn kôrlen}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\bn{নিয়ন্ত্রণ} \bn{করা}} (\emph{niyôntrôn kôrā}) is Sanskrit \emph{niyantraṇa}, restraining or governing (Monier-Williams), with \bn{করা}: to keep a crowd, a price or a feeling in check.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{niyôntrôn kôrā}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{niyôntrôn kôrā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{rāg niyôntrôn nā kôrle bipôd hôbe.} — If you don't control your anger, there will be trouble.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Bengali for to resist, then the Bengali for to ward off, then say \emph{niyôntrôn kôrā} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \bn{নিয়ন্ত্রণ} \bn{করা} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To control\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{নজর} (nôjôr)}{নজর (nôjôr)}]{\bn{নজর} (nôjôr) — watch; a close eye (on something)}

\label{lesson:BN-C374-nojor}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Bengali for to ward off, then the Bengali for to control.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{নজর}}
\textbf{\bn{নজর}} — \emph{nôjôr} — \textquotedblleft{}watch; a close eye (on something)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\bn{বাজারে} \bn{গেলে} \bn{ব্যাগের} \bn{ওপর} \bn{নজর} \bn{রাখো।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{bājāre gele byāger opôr nôjôr rākho.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
If you go to the market, keep an eye on your bag.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\bn{নজর}} (\emph{nôjôr}) is usually traced to Arabic \emph{naẓar}, a look, through Persian. \bn{নজর} \bn{রাখা} is to keep watch on something.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{nôjôr}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{nôjôr}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{bājāre gele byāger opôr nôjôr rākho.} — If you go to the market, keep an eye on your bag.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Bengali for to ward off, then the Bengali for to control, then say \emph{nôjôr} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \bn{নজর} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Watch; a close eye (on something)\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
